suite_baseline: AI Governance Suite v3.9.10 (52 artefacts, AIG-xx IDs), Playbook AIG-GOV-02
mapping_basis: Each mapping was checked against the full text of the 52-artefact suite uploaded on 11 October 2026 and updated for suite v3.9.10 (12 October 2026 data governance links). 'mapped' means the suite contains a designed control that would have caught the failure before harm; 'partial' means the risk is named but no control or measure acts on it; 'unmapped' means no artefact addresses it. All controls are design-stage: nothing is evidenced until operated.

determination_levels.alleged: Reported by media or a database; no authority has made a finding. Default for every AI Incident Database record.
determination_levels.acknowledged: The deployer admitted the failure or withdrew the system, but no court, regulator or ombudsman made a finding.
determination_levels.determined: A court, regulator or ombudsman made a finding.

failure_modes.label: Biased or discriminatory outcome
failure_modes.description: The system produced outcomes that disadvantaged people by a protected characteristic or a proxy for one.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Equality Impact Assessment before approval; bias and fairness monitoring after go-live.

failure_modes.label: Opaque decision nobody could explain
failure_modes.description: People affected could not find out that AI was used or why it reached its output.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Transparency Policy, ATRS Record and Model Card.

failure_modes.label: Unlawful or excessive personal data processing
failure_modes.description: Personal data was collected, inferred, kept or shared without a lawful basis or beyond what was needed.
failure_modes.coverage_note: DPIA per use (UC-ID) before processing starts. Since v3.9.10 the DPIA and the Intake Form both record the record of processing (ROPA) reference.

failure_modes.label: Security compromise of or through the AI
failure_modes.description: The system was attacked, manipulated or used to leak data: prompt injection, jailbreak, poisoning or model theft.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Security Review Checklist including agent threats; logging and incident detection controls.

failure_modes.label: Poor or unsuitable data
failure_modes.description: Training or input data was wrong, outdated, unrepresentative or not fit for the purpose.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Data quality requirements, data lineage standard and the Source Assurance and Traceability Register. Since v3.9.10 a Data Steward (AIG-AIMS-04 ROL-20) looks after data quality and lineage for each AI system, the AI Register links each system to its Information Asset Register entry (AIG-INV-04 column AA), and ISO/IEC 5259 and DAMA-DMBOK are recorded as voluntary references (AIG-AIMS-05 REQ-057, REQ-058).

failure_modes.label: Performance failure or drift
failure_modes.description: The system did not work reliably, or got worse over time, and nobody noticed in time.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Performance monitoring, drift detection and the Post-Deployment Monitoring Log.

failure_modes.label: Hallucination or false content
failure_modes.description: Generative output presented as fact was invented or wrong, and reached people or official records.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Generative AI guidance: human check before release and labelling of AI-generated content.

failure_modes.label: Automation bias and over-reliance
failure_modes.description: People deferred to the AI output instead of exercising their own judgement.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Human oversight controls and the human accountability principles.

failure_modes.label: No accountable owner
failure_modes.description: No one was clearly responsible for the system, its outcomes or stopping it.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Named Service Owner per AIR-ID, Terms of Reference and the Governance Decision Record.

failure_modes.label: Supplier opacity or failure
failure_modes.description: A third-party supplier's system failed, or the supplier would not disclose how it worked.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Procurement and supplier governance policy and the Supplier Due Diligence Questionnaire.

failure_modes.label: Unregistered or unauthorised use (shadow AI)
failure_modes.description: Staff used AI tools the organisation did not know about or had not approved.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Staff Guide, low-friction disclosure, retrospective intake and the AI Register.

failure_modes.label: Deployed without assessment
failure_modes.description: The system went live before its risks and impacts were assessed or tested.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Gate Map and Gate Log: no use proceeds without intake and the required delegated decision.

failure_modes.label: Solely automated significant decision
failure_modes.description: A decision with legal or similarly significant effect on a person was made by the system without meaningful human involvement.
mit_cues: loss of human agency and autonomy
failure_modes.coverage_note: Statutory-decision escalation trigger, DPIA covering UK GDPR Articles 22A to 22D, and the Contestability and Redress Control.

failure_modes.label: Harm to vulnerable people
failure_modes.description: Children, disabled people, older people, claimants, tenants, patients or others in a vulnerable position were harmed.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Vulnerable-residents escalation trigger, Human Rights Assessment and the Fundamental Rights Coverage Crosswalk.

failure_modes.label: Agent acted beyond its authority
failure_modes.description: An AI agent took actions (sending, deleting, buying, changing records) beyond what anyone approved.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Seventh escalation trigger (action without per-action human review), Agent Record, Authority Graph and Action Decision Record.

failure_modes.label: Supplier changed the model underneath
failure_modes.description: A supplier updated or swapped the underlying model and behaviour changed without the deploying organisation reassessing it.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Now covered: material supplier or model change is an escalation trigger (minimum High), the Supplier DDQ asks how changes will be notified (Q7.1 and change-control annex), and the Model Card keeps a change history. Residual risk: detection still relies on the supplier telling the council; a silent change is only caught if post-deployment monitoring notices the behaviour shift.

failure_modes.label: Reused for a purpose nobody assessed (function creep)
failure_modes.description: A system approved for one purpose was quietly used for another, or its outputs were shared onward.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Now covered: every materially distinct use gets its own UC-ID and approval applies only to the scope decided; the Statement of Applicability (A.9.4) requires scope-creep detection and reapproval; AIMS scope assigns downstream-use responsibility when the council provides AI to others.

failure_modes.label: Deskilling and lost fallback capability
failure_modes.description: Staff lost the skill or capacity to do the work without the AI, so failure or withdrawal left no safe fallback.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Partial: §4.3.13 names degraded manual fallback as a risk and the Rollout Plan records a fallback, but nothing measures whether staff can still do the work unaided. AIMS-10 measure M-10 covers AIMS role competence only.

failure_modes.label: Cumulative harm to the same people
failure_modes.description: Several individually acceptable systems combined to burden the same residents or communities.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Partial: the portfolio view (§4.5.8, Capabilities and System Map, measure M-16) tracks risk concentration on the council's side, such as supplier dependency. It does not look across systems at whether the same residents or communities are carrying the combined burden.

failure_modes.label: No route to challenge or redress
failure_modes.description: People harmed had no effective way to contest the outcome, get it corrected or be compensated.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Now covered: the Contestability and Redress Control applies wherever AI made or materially influenced a decision, routed through the council complaints procedure.

failure_modes.label: AI used to monitor or manage staff
failure_modes.description: AI monitored, scored, scheduled or disciplined workers, with harm to them as employees rather than as service users.
failure_modes.coverage_note: Unmapped: a search of all 52 artefacts found nothing on AI used to monitor or manage council staff. The suite governs AI as it affects residents; the council as employer is not covered.

mit_note: MIT risk tags are not used for deskilling, cumulative harm or staff monitoring: the nearest MIT categories (devaluation of human effort, power centralisation, employment quality) cover creative-work, market-competition and labour-market incidents, which are different failures. Checked against the first real collection on 11 Oct 2026.
